He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana Hoosiers]] from 2015 to 2017.{{cite web|first=Zach|last=Osterman|title=New IU big man Bryant: 'He can do just about everything'|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/college/indiana/2015/04/17/thomas-bryant-indiana-iu-commit-recruit-mcdonalds-all-american-tom-crean-hoosiers/25929417/|work=[[IndyStar]]|date=April 17, 2015|access-date=October 27, 2015}} Bryant was a member of the [[2022–23 Denver Nuggets season|Denver Nuggets]] team that won the [[2023 NBA Finals]]. ==High school career== Bryant played basketball at [[Bishop Kearney High School (Irondequoit, New York)|Bishop Kearney]], where as a sophomore he led his team to a 17–8 record, the 2013 New York Class AA Tournament crown, and the New York Federation Tournament of Champions.{{cite web|title=Bishop Kearney boys win state basketball title|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2013/bishop-kearney-boys-win-state-basketball-title|publisher=USA Today High School Sports|date=March 17, 2013|access-date=March 17, 2013}} After his sophomore year, Bryant transferred to [[Huntington Prep School]] in [[Huntington, West Virginia]] during the 2014 school year. As a junior, he averaged 13.9 points, 12.9 rebounds and 2.8 blocks per game.{{cite web|title=Thomas Bryant Junior year Stats|url=https://www.maxpreps.com/m/athlete/thomas-bryant/vKN1YhGKEeOZ5AAmVebBJg/basketball-winter-13-14/stats.htm|website=MaxPreps.com|date=January 7, 2014|access-date=January 7, 2014}} While there, he played on the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, Team SCAN on the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] Circuit.{{cite web|first=Thad|last=Novak|title=NCAA Basketball Recruiting: What Each 5-star Must Prove at 2014 Nike Peach Jam|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2133050-ncaa-basketball-recruiting-what-each-5-star-must-prove-at-2014-nike-peach-jam|work=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=July 17, 2014|access-date=May 25, 2020}} On January 3, 2015, Bryant scored 23 points and 12 rebounds in a 89–49 win over Whitney Young.{{cite web|first=Grant|last=Traylor|title=HPrep flies past Whitney Young|url=https://www.herald-dispatch.com/sports/high_school_sports/hprep-flies-past-whitney-young/article_e06677c0-4bc6-5884-ab0c-dd1cdd917904.html|website=Herald-Dispatch.com|date=January 4, 2015|access-date=May 25, 2020}} As a senior, Bryant averaged 17.3 points, 11.6 rebounds, 4.5 blocks and 2.5 steals per game. He was ranked the 20th-best recruit in the 2015 class by [[ESPN]] and was recruited heavily by many schools, including [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] and other power conference schools.{{cite web|title=Thomas Bryant|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/160060|website=ESPN.com|access-date=December 14, 2024}} However, his final decision came down to Indiana and Syracuse. According to Bryant's mother, who was heavily in favor of Syracuse, " [he] picked Indiana because Syracuse's basketball program was in chaos." While Bryant was trying to decide which school to attend, Syracuse was in the middle of an NCAA investigation, which eventually led to the loss of 12 scholarships over the next four years, 108 vacated wins, and [[Jim Boeheim]] being suspended for the first 9 games of the 2015–16 [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] season.{{cite web|first=Mike|last=Waters|title=Thomas Bryant talks about picking Indiana over Syracuse: 'I'm the person going to college'|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2015/04/thomas_bryant_talks_about_picking_indiana_over_syracuse_im_the_person_going_to_c.html|website=Syracuse.com|date=April 18, 2015|access-date=October 27, 2015}} Bryant's final verbal commitment to Indiana was televised live on April 4, 2015, during the Dick's Sporting Goods National Tournament on [[ESPN]].{{cite web|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|title=Indiana adds 22nd-ranked Thomas Bryant to recruiting class|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/12617709|website=ESPN.com|date=April 4, 2015|access-date=May 25, 2020}} During the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American Game]], Bryant scored 9 points and grabbed 3 rebounds in 16 minutes of play for the East team.{{cite web|title=Thomas Bryant scores 9 in McDonald's All-American Game|url=http://www.democratandchronicle.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/04/02/thomas-bryant-basketball-huntington-prep-bishop-kearney/70828558/|work=[[Democrat and Chronicle]]|date=April 2, 2015|access-date=October 27, 2015}} He was the fifth consecutive McDonald's All-American [[Tom Crean (basketball)|Tom Crean]] was able to recruit to play at IU. ==College career== [[File:Thomas Bryant.jpg|150px|thumb|left|Bryant in 2017]] Bryant had a break out performance in an 86–65 win against [[2015–16 Creighton Bluejays men's basketball team|Creighton]]. He recorded 17 points, 7 rebounds and 4 blocks in the Hoosiers win. Bryant contributed 19 points and five rebounds in a win over [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] in the NCAA tournament. Bryant averaged 11.9 points and 5.8 rebounds per game as a freshman. After the season, Bryant was named both Big Ten All-Freshman team as well as third-team [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]].{{cite web|title=Big Ten unveils Men's Basketball Postseason honors on BTN|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030716aad.html|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]|date=March 7, 2016|access-date=May 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160308103727/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030716aad.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 8, 2016}} Bryant announced his return for his sophomore year. His shooting percentage declined as a sophomore, but Bryant averaged 12.6 points, 6.6 rebounds and 1.5 blocks per game.{{cite news|first=Charlie|last=DiSturco|title=5 things to know about Thomas Bryant, the Wizards' newest addition|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/washington/wizards/5-things-know-about-thomas-bryant-wizards-newest-addition|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=July 2, 2018|access-date=September 6, 2018}} Bryant was projected as a possible top 5 pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] heading into the season along with teammate [[OG Anunoby]]. ==Professional career== ===Los Angeles / South Bay Lakers (2017–2018)=== On June 22, 2017, Bryant was drafted 42nd overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]]. He was later traded along with the 30th pick, [[Josh Hart]], to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for the Lakers' 28th pick, [[Tony Bradley (basketball)|Tony Bradley]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Acquire Josh Hart, Thomas Bryant in Trade with Utah|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170622-hart-bryant-acquired|website=NBA.com|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=July 5, 2026|last=Kioski|first=Nick}} On July 30, 2017, Bryant signed his rookie-scale contract with the Lakers.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Thomas Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/170730-thomas-bryant-signs|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 5, 2026|date=July 30, 2017}} After his one season with the team, on June 30, 2018, the Lakers waived Bryant.{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Thomas Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/180630-lakers-waive-thomas-bryant|website=NBA.com|date=June 30, 2018|access-date=June 30, 2018|last=Kioski|first=Nick}} The Lakers frequently assigned Bryant to their [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate, the [[South Bay Lakers]], during the season. Following the 2017–18 season, he was named to the All-NBA G League First Team.{{cite web|title=MVP Lorenzo Brown Headlines 2017–18 All-NBA G League First Team|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/mvp-lorenzo-brown-headlines-2017-18-all-nba-g-league-first-team/|website=NBA.com|date=April 16, 2018|access-date=December 14, 2024|url-status=dead}} ===Washington
